decision: D01 Retain the complete official project-local pstack installation
why: The requested installer created agent-specific copies; normalizing them would change its output
result: 47 skills installed; 55 trees retained

decision: D02 Stop architect at design selection and use existing independent reports
why: The assignment is specification-only and prohibits delegation
result: selected; no application implemented

decision: D03 Select one hosted modular center with PostgreSQL over chat-host sidecar or distributed actors
why: Conversation, permissions, runs, and approvals need one transaction authority
result: selected

decision: D04 Release local owner-machine execution before project creation and cloud execution
why: Prove the common contract first without changing the cloud target
result: S1 local; S2 cloud

decision: D05 Use hosted browser plus outbound CLI and defer desktop/PWA
why: Shared invitation and deployment require no privileged browser or client updater
result: selected

decision: D06 Keep project/general rooms and threads; defer direct messages and reactions
why: An explicit shared audience keeps answers and observer scope understandable
result: selected

decision: D07 Adopt the specified React/Vite/TanStack Node22/Hono/Zod PostgreSQL16/Drizzle stack
why: Accepted defaults fit one typed service with portable workers and lexical search
result: selected; patches locked during U01

decision: D08 Use Better Auth with verified-email invitations and custom roles plus project grants
why: Auth plumbing does not supply project authorization or safe invitation policy by itself
result: selected

decision: D09 Distinguish human ownership from agent identity and inactive project-main slots
why: Persistent identity need not mean permanent process or accountable agent
result: selected

decision: D10 Filter context by requester, agent, selection, and destination audience
why: A privileged requester must not cause an answer to leak into a wider room
result: selected

decision: D11 Separate task, run, session, lease, environment, approval, and publication state
why: Flags would conflate execution success with authority and delivery
result: selected

decision: D12 Use per-stream transactional counters, snapshots, and cursor replay
why: Timestamps and socket delivery do not prove durable order
result: selected

decision: D13 Use receipts and outbox reconciliation rather than exactly-once claims
why: External effects can succeed before their response or local receipt arrives
result: selected

decision: D14 Fence every worker write with run, machine, lease, and deployment epoch
why: A stale worker or restored server cannot retain publication authority
result: selected

decision: D15 Set 15-second heartbeat, 60-second lease, 30-minute run, and bounded retries
why: Concrete defaults make loss and cancellation testable without unbounded work
result: design budgets; not measured

decision: D16 Require explicit own-machine and repository matching with no fallback
why: An absent or wrong machine must not execute work elsewhere
result: selected

decision: D17 Allocate private-mirror task worktrees and isolate execution from Git credentials
why: Worktrees share refs and Git locks do not prevent writes
result: selected

decision: D18 Start with a host-owned bounded OpenAI Responses headless adapter
why: Fixed tools keep provider keys and host shell authority outside task execution
result: selected; no provider trial claimed

decision: D19 Use restricted Dev Containers and pinned OCI images as environment truth
why: Host hooks and image metadata can otherwise bypass isolation; snapshots capture incidental state
result: selected

decision: D20 Select E2B behind the runtime-neutral adapter with a live conformance gate
why: Custom image/template and network controls fit the contract without building a microVM fleet
result: selected; implementation conformance required

decision: D21 Deny egress by default and reject forbidden allow-rule overlaps
why: Provider defaults allow internet and allow rules can beat deny rules
result: selected

decision: D22 Use approved private-repository proposals and journaled provisioning
why: A crash or name collision must not create duplicate or delete unrelated resources
result: selected

decision: D23 Detect overlap and reverify every rebased exact head
why: Clean Git merge and old-head checks do not prove semantic compatibility
result: selected

decision: D24 Require non-author publication approval plus local credential-owner confirmation
why: Approval of a result is different from granting use of a person's credential
result: selected

decision: D25 Keep review and merge human-owned in all three stages
why: Published automation precedents do not establish calibrated safe automatic merge here
result: automatic merge not authorized

decision: D26 Separate owner-attested worker evidence from trusted CI
why: A valid device signature cannot prove a compromised machine ran honest tests
result: selected

decision: D27 Map missing/unavailable/skipped/neutral required checks to failure
why: GitHub accepts skipped and neutral statuses unless the aggregate refuses them
result: selected

decision: D28 Require platform and per-project live verification with retained artifacts
why: A passing orchestration test does not prove the application worked
result: selected

decision: D29 Keep decisions verbatim and knowledge reviewed, scoped, versioned, and invalidatable
why: Conversation or stored memory does not become current truth by repetition
result: selected

decision: D30 Activate project main agents in S2 and observer proposals in S3
why: Persistent context follows a proven execution record; observers cannot activate their own claims
result: selected

decision: D31 Use PostgreSQL lexical retrieval before embeddings or semantic judges
why: Jev and memory products do not establish Agora-specific accuracy or authority
result: selected

decision: D32 Use one Compose/Caddy cloud host with off-host encrypted backups and epoch-fenced restore
why: Small-team simplicity is acceptable only with a tested recovery boundary
result: selected; restore targets unmeasured

decision: D33 Define explicit retention, cost reservations, alerts, and cold-start limits
why: Unbounded artifacts, model calls, and orphan environments need enforceable ceilings
result: design budgets; not vendor guarantees

decision: D34 Render generated external links as text and quarantine active artifacts
why: Prompt injection can exfiltrate through rendered links even without a fetch tool
result: selected

decision: D35 Define 17 delivery units and 51 dependency-aware tasks with ten live lanes each
why: Each change needs a demonstrable outcome and its own evidence before dependents advance
result: plan checker initially reports 17 sections and 0 problems

decision: D36 Limit the S3 Slack bridge to approved one-way notifications
why: A second chat transport must not become a second authorization plane
result: selected

decision: D37 Separate prepublication evidence from postpublication trusted CI
why: Requiring remote CI before its enabling draft push would deadlock publication
result: clarified; local pass permits draft, not merge

decision: D38 Issue a fresh short-lived publication capability after terminal execution
why: A released execution lease cannot authorize the separately approved later effect
result: clarified; five-minute capability with stepwise authority checks

decision: D39 Make RunSpec, activity variants, payload ceilings, and execution limits explicit
why: Implementers need closed protocol shapes and enforceable budgets rather than unspecified bounded work
result: specified; limits remain design targets

decision: D40 Establish the managed-project fixture before its early dependent lanes
why: U06/U07 must not depend on the later publication broker or bypass onboarding gates
result: U01 now owns fixture CLI, image, reviewed CI, and human-owned repository prerequisites

decision: D41 Clarify canonical payloads, effective write scope, and source-tree evidence integrity
why: Different serializers, post-test mutations, and ambiguous path promises can invalidate authority or proof
result: RFC 8785 hashing and pre/post-scenario source integrity required

decision: D42 Bind required check publication to a project-dedicated checks-only App from S1
why: The generic GitHub Actions App identity cannot distinguish a trusted default-branch reporter from another workflow
result: human-installed per-project reporter; no code or provisioning permission; reporter never executes candidate code

decision: D43 Accept the specification validation with explicit vendor and product limits
why: Document consistency and planning-tool tests passed; these are not live product evidence and upstream bytes must remain intact
result: 17 plan sections; 51 tasks; 52 bundled tests; 9 checker cases; 55 retained upstream EOF warnings

decision: D44 Retain React TypeScript and Node after independent alternatives review, superseding D07 rationale
why: Both reviews covered broader alternatives including Svelte; no benchmark winner was established and the comparative Vue gate was withdrawn before implementation
result: selected renderer; ordinary production fitness remains; no competing prototypes

decision: D45 Make OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema 2020-12 authoritative, superseding shared-Zod wire authority
why: Native and other-language consumers must not depend on an internal validator or lossy export
result: generate TypeScript and Swift plus conformance fixtures; Zod internal only

decision: D46 Add framework-free client core and mechanical import boundaries
why: Replaceable rendering and service implementations require actual isolation of state, types and SDKs
result: dependency lint and forbidden-import negatives in U01a

decision: D47 Add a native public-client OAuth device boundary separate from worker enrollment
why: A native human client needs scoped credentials and recent-auth approval without a browser cookie jar or worker authority
result: S1 Swift fixture; audience/scopes, rotation, revocation and exact-action step-up

decision: D48 Separate native client distribution from native macOS execution targets
why: A Mac hosting a Linux container cannot prove Xcode, SwiftUI, AppKit or macOS packaging
result: target/capability matrix; native coding runner unavailable until separately qualified

decision: D49 Distribute the worker as a standalone protocol client with embedded runtime
why: Local installation should not require Node or center-internal TypeScript imports
result: signed Linux/macOS executables; other-language implementations use same conformance suite

decision: D50 Replace vendor-shaped execution with neutral ModelAdapter and AgentAdapter contracts, superseding D18
why: Provider-specific streaming or tool behavior cannot become the product authority model
result: two approved real provider targets plus deterministic/external-process negatives

decision: D51 Adopt Node 24 LTS and PostgreSQL 18 with dated pins, superseding D07 runtime versions
why: Current supported foundation versions and declared peer compatibility are stronger defaults than copied older majors
result: 24.21.0 and 18.6 selected; runtime compatibility remains a U01a gate

decision: D52 Require behavioral test-first and guard-negative proof regardless of expensive setup
why: The bundled TDD skill is optional in cases where this product needs an executable test route first
result: red/green identities, guard-disabled red, feature-map drift and evidence negatives mandatory

decision: D53 Split foundation milestones and close tasks on their own proof, superseding the D40 unit shape
why: A task waiting for a milestone that needs its dependent tasks deadlocks a literal scheduler
result: U01a-U01d; combined task/milestone graph and exact Outcome-to-Build ownership

decision: D54 Make project semantic and runtime readiness authoritative, superseding literal-model lane authority
why: The unchanged upstream checker measures formatting and cannot establish real verification capability
result: ten scenarios retained; no required verifier model or optional-test bypass

decision: D55 Decouple knowledge and observer work from cloud execution
why: Persistent reviewed context works on an existing registered project without a sandbox account
result: U13 after S1; U15 after U13; cloud track independent

decision: D56 Add explicit native Swift client and real external-agent tasks, superseding indefinite D05/D18 deferrals
why: Native and bring-your-agent boundaries need named outcomes and acceptance rather than an open usage trigger
result: S2 U18 AC25 and U19 AC26; no general native coding runner implied

decision: D57 Assign S1 decisions and minimal project lifecycle before their consumers
why: Read-only cited answers and task cancellation must use real earlier capabilities, not hidden fixtures or S2-only controls
result: human decisions U03; registered pause/resume/archive U02

decision: D58 Reproduce and gate task Outcome-to-Build mismatch
why: The previous public design-check command accepted an unrelated task outcome with exit zero
result: red observed before validator changes; revised gate rejects mismatches and unowned work

decision: D59 Pin a compatible TypeScript compiler rather than copying the bundled toolchain
why: openapi-typescript 7.13.0 declares a 5.x peer range, while vendored pstack uses an independent TypeScript 7 toolchain
result: TypeScript 5.9.3 candidate; full generated-client and runtime matrix required

decision: D60 Separate worker, trusted CI and non-production fixture evidence authority
why: Foundation tests must not require a finished scheduler, and independent CI cannot reuse a terminal execution lease
result: closed subject purposes; project-bound CI signing plus App/workflow receipt; fixture proof cannot publish

decision: D61 Accept revised design semantics while keeping runtime foundation unqualified
why: Reproduced validator gaps now fail closed; source checks and document/tool tests do not prove application behavior
result: 24 requirements; 26 criteria; 22 milestones; 66 tasks; 23 validator cases; 52 bundled tests; installer unchanged

decision: D62 Verify the foundation on Node 24.16.0 and PostgreSQL 18.4 and keep the dated 24.21.0/18.6 pins as deployment targets
why: The bootstrap host has those minors inside the pinned majors; clean install, strict gates, migrations and real RLS/race/rollback tests passed there, and no incompatibility was reproduced that would justify a downgrade
result: verified minors recorded; later minors unexercised

decision: D63 Record behavioral red by applying the head test patch to a test-only harness revision that serves liveness only
why: R22 forbids missing-infrastructure red; the harness proves the driver and a baseline operation, so the fixture assertions fail as 404 versus 200/400/503 at the parent
result: red exit 1 with literal assertions; green exit 0

decision: D64 Write the foundation fixture migration as reviewed SQL under the Drizzle journal and use explicit SQL for the counter and claim paths
why: R03 reserves explicit SQL for claims and counters, and no typed query path exists yet to justify a Drizzle table schema
result: migrate twice no-op with stable digest; RLS on the non-owner role

decision: D65 Cross the R11 default size target for the repository bootstrap and stop below the block threshold
why: Creating the workspace, gates, PostgreSQL path and fixture in one task is the declared Build outcome; the code diff is 999 lines across 36 files with 16 source files, and the follow-up commit adds only evidence and docs
result: scope rationale recorded; non-author approval remains with the merge authority

decision: D66 Accept the first exact-head review as FAIL and land its fixes as separate reviewed commits before recording task evidence
why: The reviewer reproduced a 500 on schema-valid UUIDs, a cross-scope event through the foreign key, a pool leak on failed rollback, pg types across the storage boundary and an owner-role probe; each fix has its own value-level red in the review round
result: fixed in 3f9aee9, db88adf, 0bddb62; second exact-head review recorded

decision: D67 Record that the review-fix commits moved the bootstrap code diff above the R11 1,000-line block threshold
why: The fixes correct the same fixture the task created, and splitting them would leave a known-broken revision on the branch; the source-file count stays below 25 and the evidence commit is prose and logs only
result: non-author size exception or split required before landing; merge authority decides

decision: D68 Firstmate, as non-author maintainer, grants a one-time R11 size exception for the bootstrap change instead of a split
why: The meaningful code addition is 1,209 lines, 209 above the hard threshold, in fewer than 25 source files for one declared bootstrap outcome; six independent review rounds corrected real defects and the final exact-head review passes; splitting the corrected fixture would add a history and evidence boundary without reducing authority or migration risk
result: approved 2026-09-20; risk class unchanged; no check waived; no precedent for later tasks

decision: D69 Author one JSON Schema 2020-12 file per wire family plus an operations-only OpenAPI 3.1.1 document, and let a project script bundle them into the one generated document both generators consume
why: swift-openapi-generator reads a single self-contained document and neither generator resolves cross-file $defs; keeping the families as the only authored schema bytes lets Ajv, the bundle, openapi-typescript and the Swift consumer derive from identical sources, and the bundler is where the tested keyword subset is enforced before any consumer exists
result: 20 components published; pnpm contracts:check rejects drift and any keyword outside the subset

decision: D70 Move RFC 8785 canonical JSON from the domain package into contracts
why: Canonical bytes are wire authority under R05 and are needed by the center, the client core, the worker and the Swift consumer; a second TypeScript canonicalizer would be a second authority. The allowed dependency direction is domain to contracts; contracts imports no domain, storage, framework or transport code
result: domain re-exports the same functions; center wire types now come only from the generated consumer

decision: D71 Publish the R12 CLI envelopes (CliCommand, CliReport, CliOutcome, ExitCode, Diagnostic, ArtifactReference, CleanupReceipt) with the foundation contract surface
why: Firstmate relayed the captain's rule that every capability stays runnable and verifiable through project-owned CLI tooling; R12 and R22 already require these shapes and later boxes consume them. Pre-envelope outputs (migration report, probe report, center start line, red-green line) stay unchanged until the agora project CLI lands in U01a.B04 and U01b
result: golden vectors cover integer limits, timestamps, closed outcomes, exit codes and command text refusal in both consumers

decision: D72 Append the CLI-operability rule to R12: every public or operator capability has a scriptable CLI or public API driver with the same authorization; a UI is never the only path
why: The existing text required the managed-project CLI contract and the agora project commands but did not state the rule for every capability or that the CLI shares the UI's authorization and transitions
result: append-only paragraph; no requirement renumbered; design gate still counts 24 requirements

decision: D73 Land U01a.B02 as three stacked fast-forward branches (harness and wiring; contract sources, generation and TypeScript consumer; golden vectors, Swift consumer and joint conformance) instead of one change
why: The combined change measured 1,238 meaningful added lines in 35 source files, above R11's 1,000-line and 25-file block; Firstmate chose the split over a second size exception because the accepted instructions make the bootstrap exception non-precedent. The harness branch is the R22 test-only revision, so each later branch's red is a value-level assertion against the previous head rather than a missing runner
result: each branch passes every applicable check at its own head; the conformance branch red and per-branch sizes are recorded under evidence/U01a/agora-s1-publish-portable-contracts/3-conformance
